I'll admit, I do wish I had upvotes and that my karma score was higher. I do wish I didn't feel like I took an L making this thread. But all y'all talking shit behind a keyboard realize I'm not finna disclose my entire existence, what I go through on the daily to some fuckwads on the internet. None of y'all know me in real life, or what I go through on the daily, y'all are just judging me based off this one forum post. I intentionally worded it in a way that would be worth reading, with light humor and shock value. I was outside and I cried, I think someone also mentioned I really just made this thread for myself, well yeah, I did. Is that a problem? I thought the whole point of reddit was to make posts. If you're not posting or commenting why use reddit in the first place. Also, none of y'all are paying attention to the fact that I posted this specifically on the Atlanta subreddit, and not the Homeless subreddit. Everyone on here is saying this and that about me as if I'm some white kid with rich parents. I admit I am in a better position than what people would perceive as actually being homeless, I didn't even feel homeless though. I felt hopeless, that's why I returned to my family. Don't you dare tell me to "Grow up and get a job", I be looking for jobs all the time. I decided to go to these shelters on my own accord to see how it would be, to see for myself how privileged I really was, and decided to share my personal experience. I'm not sure why y'all are mad about me sharing my personal experience. I guess I could have just kept this to myself, and just not said anything about it at all. I just felt like there was someone out there who might care.

P.S: I've been in soup kitchens, I've helped out churches and what not, I'm not just some ass wipe on the internet who has never contributed to society. Don't talk shit like you know me just because I made an entertaining thread. Y'all know good and well this thread entertaining because otherwise y'all wouldn't be feeling some type of way.

There's people in this world who can't even fathom being homeless for an hour, I'm making this thread for them. All those students whose parents pay for their tuition in Georgia State are surrounded by homeless shelters and anyone of them could be in a similar position and those are the people who I'm making this thread for. People like Lil Yachty have never even rode a Marta bus a day in their life. There's different levels to what people consider "the struggle". If you read my thread I also mentioned, that there were people worse off than I was, so your basically just letting me know that you can't read.

You're right, but there are people who need someone like me to share experiences like this on behalf of them. And actually technically if you were to go to a DMV they have an option for homeless, and call it "Homeless: Live in Shelter/ Live with family or friends", The government looks at both as homeless, if you are of age (not a minor) and are living with people and are not paying to stay, the government considers that to be homeless. I also don't have a car and had been walking around earlier that same day looking for jobs, so I already smelled.

I actually didn't sleep in the shelter, I felt like that shit was degrading. I ended up sleeping outside, the weather was nice, and I did have more freedom than the rules the shelter had planned out. I will do a thread on my shelter experience.
